chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Hassam, from [Ibn] Abi Shu'bah, from Abdullah ibn Ghaliib, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and recited for him the elegy of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). When I reached this verse: 'What a great disaster! Instead of scattering dust over Husayn, he was rolled in the dust!' a woman who was crying from behind the curtain screamed, 'O father!'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْن: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مِسْقَاة: A place of pouring or scattering

ai.seo_question: What happened when Imam al-Sadiq heard an elegy about Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the early tradition of *marthiyyah* (elegiac poetry) as a vehicle for transmitting the emotional reality of Karbala, linking the reciter’s performance directly to the spiritual presence of the Imams. The weeping woman behind the curtain (*khalf al-sitr*) symbolizes the hidden yet palpable connection between the living and the martyred, reinforcing the Shia concept of *mawaddah* (affection) as a tangible, affective duty. This incident underscores how poetic recitation serves not merely as remembrance but as a means of activating the spiritual lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt.
